_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Based on games-standalone terraria/vanilla/egg-terraria-vanilla.json (pelican-eggs, MIT licence). Octail changes the install script (a version downloads terraria.org's terraria-server-<number>.zip directly instead of scraping the wiki, every step is checked and failures exit non-zero; Re-Logic publishes no checksum) and adds the terraria tag, generic TCP idle sleep (off until staff enable it per server), a broadcast command, install sandbox defaults and resource hints, and spells the NPC stream rule `integer` (upstream `int` is not a Laravel rule).
name: Terraria Vanilla
author: iamkubi@gmail.com
description: Dig, fight, explore, build! Nothing is impossible in this action-packed adventure game.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Vanilla Installation Script (pelican-eggs, changed for Octail: downloads over HTTPS from terraria.org, every step
# checked, failures exit non-zero; Re-Logic publishes no checksum for the server zip)
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
set -euo pipefail
## install packages to get version and download links
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq curl unzip jq ca-certificates > /dev/null

mkdir -p /mnt/server/
cd /mnt/server/

VERSION="${TERRARIA_VERSION:-latest}"
if [ "$VERSION" = "latest" ]; then
    ## terraria.org lists the current server zip (terraria-server-<number>.zip)
    FILE=$(curl -fsSL https://terraria.org/api/get/dedicated-servers-names | jq -r '.[0] // empty' || true)
else
    ## 1.4.4.9 or 1449 → terraria-server-1449.zip
    FILE="terraria-server-$(echo "$VERSION" | tr -d '.').zip"
fi
if ! echo "$FILE" | grep -Eq '^terraria-server-[0-9]+\.zip$'; then
    echo "Installation failed: the Terraria server version couldn't be read from terraria.org."
    exit 1
fi
DOWNLOAD_LINK="https://terraria.org/api/download/pc-dedicated-server/${FILE}"
NUMBER=$(echo "$FILE" | grep -Eo '[0-9]+')

echo "Downloading ${DOWNLOAD_LINK}"
if ! curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "/mnt/server/${FILE}" "$DOWNLOAD_LINK"; then
    rm -f "/mnt/server/${FILE}"
    echo "Installation failed: terraria.org has no ${FILE} (check the version: https://terraria.wiki.gg/wiki/Server#Downloads)."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Unpacking server files"
rm -rf "/mnt/server/${NUMBER}"
if ! unzip -q -o "/mnt/server/${FILE}" "${NUMBER}/Linux/*" -d /mnt/server; then
    rm -rf "/mnt/server/${FILE}" "/mnt/server/${NUMBER}"
    echo "Installation failed: ${FILE} has no Linux server."
    exit 1
fi
cp -R "/mnt/server/${NUMBER}/Linux/." /mnt/server/
rm -rf "/mnt/server/${NUMBER}" "/mnt/server/${FILE}"
if [ ! -f /mnt/server/TerrariaServer.bin.x86_64 ]; then
    echo "Installation failed: TerrariaServer.bin.x86_64 is missing after unpacking ${FILE}."
    exit 1
fi
chmod +x TerrariaServer.bin.x86_64

## Octail sets the world, port, players, MOTD, seed and password in it before every start
echo "Generating config file"
cat <<EOF > serverconfig.txt
worldpath=/home/container/saves/Worlds
worldname=default
world=/home/container/saves/Worlds/default.wld
difficulty=3
autocreate=1
port=7777
maxplayers=8
EOF

mkdir -p /mnt/server/saves/Worlds

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed: Terraria server ${NUMBER}."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Terraria version
variables.description: latest (the current server on terraria.org), or a version as its full number or its file number, such as 1.4.4.9 or 1449 (https://terraria.wiki.gg/wiki/Server#Downloads). Players need the same version. Reinstall to switch.

variables.name: World Name
variables.description: The name for the world file.

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: The maximum number of players a server will hold.

variables.name: World Seed
variables.description: The Seed to use when creating the World

variables.name: Password
variables.description: The password which should be used.

variables.name: NPCStream
variables.description: Reduces enemy skipping but increases bandwidth usage. The lower the number the less skipping will happen, but more data is sent. 0 is off.
